outgoing.name: Belgium
outgoing.excerpt: Remains of the best-known Iguanodon species have been found predominantly in Belgium, England, Germany, Spain and France.

outgoing.name: Brussels
outgoing.excerpt: The completed restoration makes an impressive display in the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences, in Brussels.

outgoing.name: Cretaceous
outgoing.excerpt: Iguanodon gives its name to the infraorder Iguanodontia, a very populous group with many species of Ornithopod from the mid-Jurassic to the Late Cretaceous.

outgoing.name: England
outgoing.excerpt: Iguanodon was the first dinosaur recognized and the second dinosaur formally named, described in 1822 by English geologist Gideon Mantell.

outgoing.name: London

outgoing.name: Mongolia
outgoing.excerpt: Remains of similar animals have been found in Tunisia and Mongolia, and distinct species have been found in Utah and South Dakota.

outgoing.name: New Zealand
